title: Top Tablets Worth Buying This Holiday Season (2026)
summary: The iPad and Samsung Galaxy Tab lines lead the tablet picks from the main review sites this year.
method: Picks come from Tom's Guide (via AOL), TechRadar, Tech Advisor and Consumer Reports' tablet testing. Only models covered by at least two of these sources are listed.
assumptions: We show no prices because tablet prices change often. Check the current price and storage size before you buy.

products.name: Apple iPad (A16)
why: TechRadar calls the latest 11-inch iPad its best budget iPad. Tom's Guide says iPadOS still has the best app library and richest feature set for tablets.
Consumer Reports includes the iPad A16 among its top tested tablets.
cons: Not as powerful as the Air or Pro
products.skip_if: You need pro-level power or a laminated, higher-end display

products.name: Apple iPad Air (M4)
why: Tech Advisor reviewed the 2026 iPad Air and found more power with the same formula. Justbuy calls the 11-inch Air a light yet powerful everyday tablet.
Parse's roundup of AI answers also names the iPad Air for overall balance.
specs: Newer chip than the base iPad
pros: More power than the base iPad
cons: Costs more than the base iPad
products.best_for: People who want a step up without paying Pro prices

products.name: Samsung Galaxy Tab S11
why: Tech Advisor calls the Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra the ultimate Android tablet, and Consumer Reports features the Galaxy Tab S11 in its top picks.
Justbuy says the Tab S11 is built for people who work on the go and want the most from the display.
specs: Ultra version is the biggest and priciest
cons: Android tablet apps are weaker than iPad apps
products.best_for: Android fans who want a premium tablet
products.skip_if: You want the biggest tablet app library

products.name: Apple iPad Pro (M5)
why: Tom's Guide says the iPad Pro M5 has possibly the best screen it has ever seen and is the first iPad with fast charging, but is overkill for most people.
Tech Advisor's review says the best comes at a cost.

products.best_for: Creators and pros who want the best iPad

products.name: Apple iPad Mini (7th Gen)
why: CNET lists the seventh-gen iPad Mini among the best tablets you can buy, noting that all iPads are top-tier options. It is highlighted as a quality choice for users who want a premium small tablet.
ZDNET includes it in their list of the best small tablets for 2026, suitable for reading, watching videos, or as a kid-friendly option. It offers rapid performance and access to favorite apps.
products.desc: The iPad Mini is a small tablet with a display size ranging from around six to 10 inches. It offers rapid performance and access to apps. It is a premium device from Apple.
products.benefit: Picture a commuter using it to read on the beach or watch videos during a long car trip. It provides a vibrant display and powerful performance that rivals larger tablets. It beats the Amazon Fire HD 10 in build quality and app ecosystem, and it is more versatile than the Ayaneo Pocket Micro for general use. The catch: It is an Apple device, so it may not be suitable for users who prefer Android or Windows.
specs: Display size: around six to 10 inches
cons: Premium price point implied by 'best' status
products.best_for: Users who want a premium, versatile small tablet for media and light productivity.
products.skip_if: You are strictly on a budget or prefer Android.

products.name: Amazon Fire HD 10
why: PCMag names the Fire HD 10 as an Editors' Choice winner and the best cheap tablet for most people. It offers the best blend of performance, price, and size in the Fire lineup.
CNET includes it in their list of top tablets, noting that affordable budget tablets are good for consuming media or playing casual games.
products.desc: The Fire HD 10 is a budget tablet designed for reading books, watching videos, and browsing the web. It is part of the Fire lineup and offers a good balance of performance and size.
products.benefit: Picture a student using it to read textbooks or watch lectures without spending a lot of money. It provides exceptional value for basic entertainment tasks. It beats the iPad Mini on price and is more focused on media consumption than the Ayaneo Pocket Micro. The catch: You must be okay with the Fire OS ecosystem, which may limit app availability compared to iOS or Android.
specs: Best blend of performance, price, and size
cons: Limited app ecosystem compared to iOS/Android
products.best_for: Budget-conscious buyers who primarily use tablets for media and web browsing.
products.skip_if: You need a full Android or iOS experience for productivity apps.
